set.body:
CORRECTNESS BUG, found independently by two reviewers and reproduced by me. Not a usability issue.

REPRODUCTION, verbatim:

  v <- rsa(g, models = list(category = cat_rdm))
  as.data.frame(v)   # correct: 6 x 3
  m <- as.matrix(v)
  dim(m)             # 6 1        <- WRONG, coefficients are 6 x 2
  class(m)           # effect_rsa_view   <- WRONG, still carries the view class
  print(m)
  #> Error in matrix(values, ncol = 1L) :
  #>   'data' must be of a vector type, was 'NULL'
  #> Calls: print ... as.data.frame.effect_rsa_view -> .bind_result_values -> matrix

WORSE THAN FIRST REPORTED. The reviewer described this as silently returning garbage. It is
worse: as.matrix.default operates on the underlying LIST, returns a 6x1 matrix, and the result
RETAINS class effect_rsa_view. So the user now holds a malformed object that claims to be a
view. Printing it dispatches to print.effect_rsa_view, which calls as.data.frame.effect_rsa_view,
which crashes inside .bind_result_values (R/format-results.R:14).

The failure is therefore delayed and misattributed. The corruption happens at as.matrix(); the
error surfaces later, at print, inside the formatting code, with a message about vector types
that names nothing the user did. A user will conclude the print method is broken, not the
coercion.

The second reviewer independently hit the identical message ('data' must be of a vector type,
was NULL) while trying to get a square RDM out, which is the natural thing to want from rdm().

SCOPE: no as.matrix method is defined for ANY of the 6 view classes (NAMESPACE registers 10
print, 10 format, 6 as.data.frame, 0 as.matrix, 0 summary, 0 plot). So every view class has this
behaviour. as.matrix() is a base generic that R users reach for reflexively on anything
tabular, and every class in this package answers it with a corrupted object.

FIX, two parts:
  1. define as.matrix methods for the view classes returning the actual value matrix
     (for effect_rdm_view the natural return is the square q x q matrix, which is what a
     user asking for as.matrix(rdm(g)) means)
  2. independently, .bind_result_values should fail with a message naming the malformed
     input rather than surfacing a base matrix() error, since that path is reachable
     from any corrupted view

SEPARABLE, from the same review and NOT a bug: no summary() and no plot() exist for any class.
Both are ordinary gaps rather than defects. If summary() is added it must state that values are
signed and may be negative, otherwise it invites reading a median as a positive quantity - which
would silently undo the package's most distinctive inferential commitment.
set.title: as.matrix() on a view returns a corrupted object of the same class that then crashes on print
